steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Qualitative data is non-numerical — it describes qualities or categories (e.g. eye colour, favourite subject). | Key Fact: Quantitative data is numerical — it can be measured or counted (e.g. height, number of pets). | Key Fact: Quantitative data splits into discrete and continuous. | Key Fact: Discrete data can only take specific values, usually whole numbers (e.g. number of siblings, shoe size).
